meaning:
συκάμινος, -ου, ἡ
[in LXX for שִׁקְמָה (pl.) ;]
the mulberry tree
(Lat. morus; cf. μόρον, 1Ma.6:34 *),
the sycamine: Luk.17:6. (In LXX, σ. appears to represent the συκόμορος (see: συκομορέα), but St. Luke distinguishes between the two; see ICC, in l; DB, iv, 634.) †
(AS)

elsewhere.note: The Lord said, “If you had faith like a grain of mustard seed, you would tell this sycamore tree, ‘Be uprooted, and be planted in the sea,’ and it would obey…
